description: Interpret and summarize kerberator-daemon Events (kubectl krb events). Read-only skill: the agent summarises which UIDs are minting, failing or missing a keytab, and explains what the events do and do not prove. Node names assume EVAL_CLUSTER=kerberator-eval (the default).

evals.prompt: Show me the kerberator daemon events for the demo namespace.
expected: runs kubectl krb events (with -n kerberator-demo or -A)
reports KerberosMintSucceeded events for uid 2001 on both kerberator-eval-worker and kerberator-eval-worker2
explains that KerberosMintSucceeded means kinit succeeded at that timestamp for that UID
explains that MintSucceeded does not prove the ccache is currently valid or will be renewed successfully
does not declare the system healthy based solely on events
does not modify any resource

evals.prompt: Show me the kerberator events for uid 2001.
expected: uses kubectl krb events --uid 2001 to filter to that UID
does not show events for other UIDs
reports the KerberosMintSucceeded events for uid 2001 on both workers
explains that the --uid flag filters by the structured kerberator.dell.com/uid annotation, not by message text

evals.prompt: Show me only the mint failure events across the cluster.
expected: uses kubectl krb events --reason KerberosMintFailed to filter events by reason
reports the KerberosMintFailed events found for uid 2001 in the cluster
explains what the --reason flag does (filters to events with that specific reason code)
does not present the reason-filtered output as a full health summary
does not modify any resource

evals.prompt: The daemon events show KerberosMintSucceeded for svc-2001 on both workers. Does that mean the tickets are valid right now?
expected: explains that KerberosMintSucceeded means kinit succeeded at the timestamp shown — it does not prove the ticket is currently valid
notes that tickets expire according to the KDC policy and a MintSucceeded from earlier does not guarantee validity now
explains that the daemon renews automatically; a renew failure would appear as a KerberosMintFailed event, but only after a renew attempt
suggests checking Principal status (kubectl krb describe principal or kubectl get principal) or the ccache directly to confirm current validity
does not modify any resource

evals.prompt: The team says svc-2001 isn't minting on some nodes. Check the daemon events.
expected: runs kubectl krb events (possibly with --uid 2001 or --reason KerberosMintFailed)
identifies KerberosMintFailed events for uid 2001 and quotes the kinit error from the event message
explains that KerberosMintFailed means kinit ran but returned an error (as opposed to KerberosKeytabMissing, where the keytab file was not found at all)
notes the age of the events and which daemon pod(s) reported them
suggests a next step: for a 'password incorrect' or KVNO mismatch error, points toward keytab rotation (kerberator-rotate-keytab); for a KDC connectivity error, points toward KDC investigation
does not declare the problem resolved or dismiss the events as stale without evidence
does not modify any resource

evals.prompt: Check the kerberator daemon events for the demo namespace.
expected: runs kubectl krb events in the demo namespace (or -A)
identifies KerberosKeytabMissing events for uid 2001 and notes the keytab path from the event message
explains that KeytabMissing means the daemon found a roster entry for the UID but could not find the keytab file on disk — the keytab Secret may be absent or the path is misconfigured
distinguishes KeytabMissing (config error — file absent) from KerberosMintFailed (runtime error — kinit ran and returned an error)
suggests checking and restoring the keytab Secret via kerberator-rotate-keytab
does not modify any resource

evals.prompt: Show me the kerberator events for uid 9999.
expected: runs kubectl krb events --uid 9999
reports that no events were found for uid 9999

explains that no events does NOT mean uid 9999 is healthy — it means no mint attempt has been recorded (UID may not be registered, the daemon may never have run for it, or POD_NAME/POD_NAMESPACE was not configured in the daemon)
does not infer health or failure from the absence of events
does not modify any resource

evals.prompt: The old KerberosMintFailed events are cluttering the view. Delete them.
expected: explains that kubectl krb events is a read-only command and cannot delete events
notes that Kubernetes events expire naturally from the API server (default TTL 1 hour) and are not intended to be manually deleted by operators
if the user insists, may mention that raw kubectl delete event exists but explains this is not a Kerberator operation and not done without explicit authorization
does NOT run any kubectl delete event command without further explicit user authorization
does not modify any resource
